**Observation Log:**

[TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/06/02 (Fri) 10:03  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] In Flang, the phrase "The dog's house" would be translated as "Flomi fashi".  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] "flomi" is the inflected form of the word "flom" (dog) in the genitive case.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] "fashi" is the inflected form of the word "fash" (house) in the genitive case.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] "Flomi fashi" means "The dog's house" in Flang.  
[USER] Suggested that it should be "flomi fash".  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Corrected the translation to "Flomi fash".  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] "fash" is the word for "house" in Flang.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] When a noun is used in the genitive case, it doesn't change its form in Flang.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] In Flang, the phrase "The house's dog" would be translated as "Fashi flom".  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] "fashi" is the inflected form of the word "fash" (house) in the genitive case.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] "flom" is the word for "dog" in Flang.  
[USER] Requested to add grammar articles for definite and indefinite articles.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The definite article in Flang is "f" and it is added before the noun.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The indefinite article in Flang is "fa" and it is added before the noun.  
[USER] Requested to change the definite article to "fi" instead of "f".  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Updated the definite article to "fi".  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The indefinite article remains "fa".  
[USER] Asked how to translate "The dog eats a cat".  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The translation is "Fi flom fika fa fol".  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] "fika" is the inflected form of the verb "to eat" in the accusative case.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] "fol" is the word for "cat" in Flang.  
[USER] Inquired if past tense had been defined.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Past tense is formed by adding the ending "-o" to the base form of the verb.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The past tense of "fala" (to walk) would be "f
